content.title: WWE WrestleMania 42 Night 2 results, grades, analysis: Roman Reigns outlasts CM Punk in thrilling WrestleMania finale
content.text: WrestleMania 42 concluded with Night 2 on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. The six-match card featured three title changes, headlined by Roman Reigns dethroning CM Punk in an epic World Heavyweight Championship match.Reigns captured one of WWE’s top championships in an instant classic against CM Punk that shakes up the landscape of "WWE Raw" for the rest of 2026. It was an excellent match all around, with intense action and drama that is needed from a WrestleMania main event. Overall, Reigns and Punk delivered on every expectation — and more.The "SmackDown" women’s division received a major shakeup as well, as Rhea Ripley defeated Jade Cargill in a very strong match for the WWE Women's Championship that proved to be the best women’s contest of the entire weekend. Cargill looked the best she has in WWE, even in defeat, and Ripley continued to add accolades and standout performances to her already impressive résumé.AdvertisementNight 2 also featured the WrestleMania debuts for two of WWE's brightest young stars, Oba Femi and Trick Williams. Femi absolutely dominated Brock Lesnar in the opening match of the night and Williams captured the United States Championship by defeating Sami Zayn later in the evening. Both were star-making performances on WWE’s biggest stage.In the aftermath of Femi’s win, longtime WWE star Brock Lesnar appeared to retire, leaving his gloves and boots in the middle of the ring and sharing an emotional moment with Paul Heyman. While there had been hints that Lesnar is nearing the end of his wrestling career, it’s unclear if this is an official retirement or if it will be part of an angle to set up an actual retirement match later this year against Gunther.AdvertisementOne of the best matches of the entire weekend came as Penta retained his Intercontinental Championship in a ladder match against five other competitors. Each man in the bout had a truly jaw-dropping moment, but no one shined brighter than Je’Von Evans, who like Femi and Williams was in his first WrestleMania. It’ll be a match we’re talking about for a long time to come.Finally, Finn Balor revived his "Demon" character in a street-fight victory over Dominik Mysterio, effectively ending Balor’s yearslong involvement with the Judgment Day faction and potentially launching him higher up the card on “Raw.”Here's a look at the full WrestleMania 42 Night 2 card:WWE WrestleMania 42 Night 2 featured six matches, including World Heavyweight Champion CM Punk defending his title against Roman Reigns. (Josh Heim, Uncrowned)Roman Reigns def. CM Punk in 33:57 to win the World Heavyweight ChampionshipGrade: A+Best spot: Punk’s big elbow through the announcers' tableAnalysis: For the second year in a row, Punk and Reigns took part in an instant-classic match at WrestleMania. The longest match on either night delivered great action and storytelling, showing why "The OTC" and "Voice of the Voiceless" are two of the best to ever step in a wrestling ring. Punk pulled out all of the stops — including a curious low blow — to try and beat Reigns, but it wasn’t enough to take him down in Reigns' 11th WrestleMania main event.Either outcome here would have kept the main-event picture on “Raw” extremely healthy, but with Reigns on top there are several feuds we can see build between Jey Uso, Finn Balor, Seth Rollins, Gunther or Bron Breakker down the line.For Punk, it’s very possible we see him take some well-deserved time off considering the schedule he’s been running and the level he has operated at for the past 18 months.AdvertisementRhea Ripley def. Jade Cargill in 10:10 to win the WWE Women's ChampionshipGrade: A-Best spot: Jade Cargill’s Sandstorm finisherAnalysis: This is the best Jade Cargill has looked in a WWE ring, so she deserves an immense amount of credit for silencing any doubters coming into WrestleMania and continuing to hone her craft at a rapid pace. If there was any question if she would rise to the occasion, it was answered very clearly on Sunday.Even though she didn’t win, I would be surprised if Cargill wasn’t in or around the main-event scene for the foreseeable future.As far as Ripley, it was another remarkable performance from one of the biggest stars in WWE today. Ripley will undoubtedly bring a much-needed shakeup to the "SmackDown" women’s division — hopefully leaving Iyo Sky to forge her own path on "Raw.""The Demon" Finn Balor def. Dominik Mysterio in 10:25Grade: B+Best spot: Balor’s Coup de Grace finishAnalysis: The fact that Balor was reprising his "Demon" character signaled he was likely to win here in what was a smart use of the Street Fight stipulation.Balor continues his strong 2026 and should be able to distance himself from the Judgment Day, likely into either the Intercontinental Championship or World Heavyweight Championship picture.Mysterio, despite taking the loss, did wonderful work in this match and continues to make a big name for himself in AAA. Mysterio is a prime candidate for a run at the Money in the Bank ladder match, which would be a really strong way to accelerate his rise to the highest levels of WWE — a position that will come at some point in his career.Trick Williams def. Sami Zayn in 7:06 to win the United States ChampionshipGrade: BBest spot: Trick Williams’ Trick ShotAnalysis: Trick Williams was seemingly destined to win here and continue his rapid ascent in WWE. Lil Yachty factoring in was always going to happen and it didn’t feel overly forced, which is a good thing but the fans didn’t seem to care at all for his involvement from the get-go.Both Williams and Zayn are capable of having a much longer, more enthralling match, so hopefully we see them run this back with a little more time and the inclusion of Carmelo Hayes. With 10 more minutes and Hayes as the third man, this could have been really elevated.Penta def. Je'Von Evans, Rusev, Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and JD McDonagh in 15:10 to retain the Intercontinental ChampionshipGrade: A+Best spot: Evans’ OG Cutter to RusevAnalysis: Much like the Jacob Fatu vs. Drew McIntyre match a night earlier, WWE couldn’t have put on a better match for the ESPN crowd. Every single competitor had a moment in a match that left you in awe, including the best spot — a stunning OG Cutter from Evans to Rusev, who was climbing a ladder.Penta keeping the championship was the best outcome here and there should be no shortage of challengers for the Lucha star, including any of his five foes in this match, who all look significantly stronger coming out of WrestleMania than they already did coming in.I firmly believe we’ll be talking about this match in November and December when we’re debating the best match of 2026.Oba Femi def. Brock Lesnar in 4:45Grade: ABest spot: Femi’s Fall From GraceAnalysis: This was exactly what it needed to be. Quick, hard-hitting and a match that cemented Femi as a monster star in WWE. It was clear from the outset how big this moment and match was for the fans, and WWE added to the big-fight feel with a Sunday run-up that lasted longer than the match itself. (Not a gripe!)Femi can enter whatever championship picture or feud he chooses now — I’d even consider having him win Money in the Bank later this year.After the match, Lesnar left his gear in the ring and appeared to retire and/or say farewell to WWE after a nearly 25-year career. Fans showered Lesnar with praise and he shared some emotional moments with Heyman and fans on his walk out of WrestleMania. There is a chance this is a semi-work for a retirement match between Lesnar and Gunther, which may be the favor Heyman owes "The Ring General."For complete updates, results and analysis from WrestleMania 42 Night 2, follow Uncrowned's live blog below:Live coverage is over74 updatesMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:42 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:30 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:29 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerAmid the carnage, Punk rolled Reigns back into the ring. The two men stared one another down again and Reigns hit another spear, with added momentum, to score the victory.Roman Reigns def. A headbutt from Punk sent both men back to their knees. Punk unwrapped his hand and threw the tape to distract the referee. He delivered a low blow to Reigns and followed up with a GTS, but Reigns kicked out.Punk kept on Reigns, dropping several elbows on him and shoving him out of the ring, setting the challenger up on the announce table again. Punk climbed to the top turnbuckle again and hit a big elbow onto Reigns through the table.Mon, April 20, 2026 at 1:26 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:23 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:20 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerReigns' abuse continued as he sent Punk crashing through the Spanish announce table with a powerbomb. Reigns, who needed to pin or submit Punk, rolled the champion back into the ring. As he went for a spear, Punk mustered up the strength to deliver a GTS to Reigns for a near-fall and send the crowd into "this is awesome" chants.Punk went for a second GTS but Reigns escaped and ducked a clothesline to set up his first spear of the match. Reigns went for the immediate pin but Punk kicked out, leaving Reigns stunned. A furious Reigns repeatedly slammed Punk's face into the canvas and taunted the champion with his "GTS" gesture. As Reigns picked up Punk and nearly connected with the move, the champion grabbed Reigns' knee and delivered a desperation kick to the head.Punk returned the favor, teasing a Superman Punch, which he connected with for a near-fall on Reigns. Punk refused to let up, punching Reigns and then going to grab an Ula Fala from a fan seated ringside. As Punk went for a spear, Reigns caught him in a guillotine choke. Punk turned it into a pin and then locked in an Anaconda Vice in the center of the ring. Reigns tried and succeeded to punch his way out, trading in for another guillotine choke.Mon, April 20, 2026 at 1:19 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:17 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:14 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:11 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerReigns looked to line Punk up for a spear, but Punk quickly hit Reigns with two running knees, clotheslines and a swinging neckbreaker. Reigns, on his heels, escaped the ring only to be met by a suicide dive from Punk. Punk kept the pressure up by bouncing Reigns' head off the announce table and steel steps.With Reigns laid out on the announce table, Punk returned to the ring and looked ready to attempt a big elbow from the ring post to table. Reigns rushed out of danger and the two men battled on the ring apron.Reigns came out on top, getting Punk hung up in a Tree of Woe. The challenger unloaded on Punk, capping it off with a trio of Superman Punches. Reigns then took the steel steps and hit Punk in the face with them, busting him open. Punk finally fell off the ring apron but endured heavy punishment.Mon, April 20, 2026 at 1:09 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:06 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerReigns took his time taunting as Punk was in the crowd, a period that allowed Punk to recover and hit a leaping tackle on the challenger. Punk then repeated that mistake as he played to the crowd and Reigns tossed him off the announce table and onto the floor.Back in the ring, Reigns won a back-and-forth sequence and went for a pin, which Punk kicked out of. Reigns got Punk hung up in between the ropes and then trapped in a corner. Reigns dished out heavy clotheslines to Punk as the crowd counted along. Reigns went for another pin after a leaping clothesline in the middle of the ring.Reigns was first to attempt a finisher, lining up a Superman Punch that Punk evaded. Punk utilized the miss to launch into an offensive flurry including a crossbody off the top rope. Punk followed up this sequence with his patented running high knee and bulldog to set up the GTS. Punk was able to get Reigns onto his shoulders but Reigns utilized elbow strikes to escape, send Punk into the ring post and land a sudden Superman Punch for a near-fall.Mon, April 20, 2026 at 1:04 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 1:00 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerReigns and Punk took in the atmosphere, letting the moment breathe by standing in their corners for a few seconds before slowly walking to the center of the ring and engaging in a staredown.After a minute, the two engaged in a collar-and-elbow, which was broken up and Punk taunted Reigns for being too oiled up. Punk followed up with a big shoulder tackle and side headlock. The crowd was divided, trading "let's go Roman" and "CM Punk" chants.Reigns' first impact move came as he hit a Samoan drop on Punk. Punk tried to fight back with a chop to Reigns and for the first time in the match, Reigns' power advantage shined through as he floored Punk with one punch. Reigns then sent Punk over the top rope out to the floor. Reigns then stalked Punk, bouncing his head off the ring post. He attempted to do the same to Punk on the announce table but Punk blocked it. Reigns rebounded quickly and whipped Punk into the barricade before breaking the referee's count.Mon, April 20, 2026 at 12:57 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 12:54 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 12:54 AM UTCMon, April 20, 2026 at 12:50 AM UTCAnthony Sulla-HeffingerLike last year, where CM Punk came out for his main-event match to "This Fire Burns," Punk got another throwback intro with "Miseria Cantare" playing during his intro montage — paying homage to his Ring of Honor days. As the music/montage stopped, Punk took at the top of the ramp in silence and with no graphics playing. As he screamed "It's Clobbering Time," "Cult of Personality" hit and the crowd erupted.
